Thornton, apparently upset with any reference to his movie career, was unresponsive to Ghomeshi's questions until the men finally declared a truce to talk about music. Billy Bob Thornton’s strange and prickly CBC radio appearance has turned from an awkward promotional stop into a full-blown touring controversy — complete with heckling Canadian concert-goers, canceled dates, and a return to the road alongside Willie Nelson.

The situation escalated when Thornton complained about Canadian audiences, suggesting they were unusually reserved. The phrase became an instant punchline, spreading across entertainment blogs and news sites as the CBC interview circulated online.

The backlash appeared to take a toll. The Boxmasters later canceled remaining Canadian dates on Nelson’s tour, with reports citing illness, though the timing fueled speculation that the hostile reception and media attention had played a role.

But the band did not stay off the road for long. The Boxmasters rejoined Willie Nelson’s tour in Connecticut, returning to the stage after the Canadian controversy had already become one of the strangest celebrity-interview sagas of the year.

For Thornton, the episode highlighted the uneasy line between Hollywood fame and musical credibility. But the CBC appearance had the opposite effect: instead of separating Thornton the musician from Thornton the actor, it ensured that both identities would be discussed together — loudly, awkwardly, and with gravy jokes attached.
